name: AI Design Architect Workspace
tag: Sketch an agent architecture, wire up its prompt flow and test it on sample inputs in one place.

scenarios.title: Design a quote-request assistant
scenarios.ask: Design an assistant that turns customer emails into draft quotes, with {nodes} prompt steps, tested on {cases} sample emails.
steps: Canvas
Drew a flow with {nodes} steps that read the email, pull out line items, look up prices and draft the quote.
Prompt editor
Wrote a prompt for each step with input and output fields named so steps connect cleanly.
Test bench
Ran {cases} sample emails. {=round(cases * min(0.95, 0.7 + nodes * 0.05))} produced a complete quote.
Inspector
Most failures came from emails listing items in a table image. Suggested an image-reading step.
followups: Why does adding steps raise the pass rate?
Each step does one small job and checks its own output, so errors are caught earlier. Past about six steps the gain is small and cost keeps rising.
Yes. Export as JSON or as Python code that runs the same prompts in the same order.

scenarios.title: Choose between two prompt versions
scenarios.ask: Test two versions of our summary prompt on {cases} support tickets and pick the better one.
steps: Test bench
Ran version A and version B on the same {cases} tickets.
Grader
Scored each summary for accuracy, missing facts and length against a {length}-word target.
Diff view
Showed the {=max(5, round(cases * 0.1))} tickets where the two versions differed most.
Recommendation
Version B wins on missing facts. Version A is closer to the length target.

result.title: A versus B
rows: B, with a stricter length instruction

followups: A grader model scores them against a rubric you can edit. Spot-check 10 by hand to make sure the grader agrees with your team.
For a clear winner, usually yes. If the scores are within two points, add more tickets before deciding.

scenarios.title: Map an agent architecture
scenarios.ask: Draw the architecture for a research agent with {tools} tools and {memory} memory.
steps: Canvas
Placed the agent, {tools} tools and a {memory} memory store on the board.
Linter
Checked every arrow has a defined input and output. Found {=max(1, round(tools / 3))} tools with no error handling.
Simulator
Walked 5 sample questions through the diagram and highlighted the path each took.
Documenter
Generated a one-page design doc from the diagram.
followups: The agent can recall earlier sessions, like a user's preferred sources. It also needs a retention rule and a way for users to clear it, which the workspace adds to the design.
Can my team comment on the diagram?
Yes. Anyone with the link can leave comments on a component.
